..
As of 330 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Above normal temperatures with dry conditions
prevail through Friday.

The latest WX analysis indicates a broad upper level ridge over
the western Gulf coast, extending NE through the TN Valley. Sfc
high pressure is centered along/or just off the coast. There is
still enough low level moisture that SCT-BKN cumulus have developed
this aftn, though this should diminish over the next few hrs
given the lower sun angle this time of year. Temperatures are
mostly in the upper 70s to lower 80s with dew pts in the lower
60s, so overall a fairly pleasant end to September for the 
local area. For tonight, expect to see a lot of high clouds 
streaming over the the upper level ridge axis, some of this is 
already seen on satellite imagery. With the sfc high drifting 
offshore, a light southerly flow is anticipated. Some patchy fog
can't be ruled out, but with the high clouds and light 
southerly flow, expect the coverage to be fairly limited (best 
chances across interior southern VA and NE NC). Lows will be in 
the upper 50s to lower 60s for most, ranging from as low as the 
mid 50s in the coolest piedmont locations to the upper 60s at 
the coast in the SE. 

The ridge shifts to the east, becoming centered across the SE
coast Thursday-Friday, allowing the sfc high to slide well 
offshore. Expect temperatures to become very warm Thursday and 
Friday as the low level S-SW flow increases; highs into the 
mid 80s to near 90F Thursday, with upper 80s to lower 90s 
Friday is about 10-15 F above average for the start of October 
and qualifies as "unseasonably warm". Have included record highs
in a Climate section for Friday since Norfolk may be close
(records are very unlikely elsewhere). 

KEY MESSAGE 2...An unsettled weather pattern with cooler and 
wetter conditions is likely for this weekend, then gradually 
drying out and remaining cool next week.

An increasingly unsettled pattern looks to take shape for the
weekend into early next week. A deep closed low currently over 
the Desert Southwest into the Intermountain West looks to open 
up on Thursday as it absorbs the mid-level remnants of TC Polo 
and lifts across the central and southern Plains. This system 
will eventually become absorbed into a northern stream trough 
digging across the interior Northeast into the northern Mid- 
Atlantic over the weekend. This will serve to dampen the 
Southeast ridge and allow an influx of Gulf and Pacific moisture
across the Gulf Coast and Mid-South, likely reaching our region
over the weekend. One signal common to all guidance, even this 
far out, is a notable increase in PWATs, with values reaching 
1.5-2.0" by Saturday night/Sunday. While some model differences
remain, trends are favoring pushing that front south through 
much of the area on Saturday, with the front then slowing or 
stalling Sat night, as additional, and likely more significant 
swaths of moisture ride along the front later in the weekend 
into early next week. While a mainly cloudy sky and some 
scattered showers are expected to accompany the initial frontal 
passage and wind shift on Saturday, the more widespread rainfall
(and bulk of the QPF) is expected Sat night through Sunday. 
Periods of rain are then likely to continue into Sunday night
before ending from NW to SE. There is still plenty of time to 
monitor the trends over the next several days, but locally heavy
rainfall is certainly possible (although much of this would be 
beneficial given ongoing drought). 12Z/30 Ensemble probs for 
1"+ of total rainfall are pushed farther north from the EPS 
(Euro) compared to the GEFS, which keeps 50% chances confined to
to southern VA and NE NC. 

In terms of temperatures, increased clouds/precip and onshore 
flow favor much cooler high temps over the weekend into early 
next week, with many areas struggling to get out of the mid-
upper 60s both Saturday and Sunday (highs generally in the 70s
across the far south). Latest models continue in good agreement
showing a strong enough push of drier air associated with high 
pressure building in from the north into the middle of next 
week, leading to below normal temperatures with highs in the 
60s and lows into the 40s and 50s Tue-Wed. The LREF robs even
show some chance for lows into the upper 30s across the NW
piedmont by Wed AM.
